div.style: width: 1920px; height: 1080px; box-sizing: border-box; padding: 80px 120px; background: #F4F5F7; color: #11151B; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 36px
display: flex; justify-content: space-between; font-family: 'IBM Plex Mono', monospace; font-size: 22px; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: #4A5361

div.h2: Two drafts, then one step out of this repository
div.p: Each draft is written against the three questions a maintainer asks.

svg.aria-label: Two drafts: the pull request description for a case, and a spec-change proposal whose worked example lets a profile's evaluation.result be an object. Then upstream.py copies the case into your fork and prints the remaining steps without touching git. Checkpoint 5 at the bottom right.

g.text: case-addition.md
The pull request description for a case. A worked
draft for the example is there; write yours.
If Lab B showed the corpus already covers your
defect, write the case-problem issue instead: does
the published case isolate it?
spec-change.md
The worked example: allow an object for a profile's
evaluation.result. W6 and W7 found it cannot hold a
suite's result without flattening it to a string.
Written to be argued with; its last section argues
with it. Then write your own.
uv run upstream.py --into <your fork of the specification> --case <your id>
copies the case into
conformance/cases/
AND PRINTS WHAT REMAINS
the checker
the generator move
the CHANGES.md bullet
the listed assemblers
the signed commit
it never touches git
the only step of this module that leaves this repository
CHECKPOINT 5 · WHAT MAKES A DRAFT READY
It names the gap or the comparison,
says whether a rule changes,
and lists what each listed assembler did.
and the thing from this repository you would propose first
